headline: Google Unveils Gemini 4 Carbon
lede: Gemini 4 Carbon targets sustained agentic work across engineering and cybersecurity. Google reports stronger vulnerability discovery, exploit validation, patching, and prompt-injection resistance, while independent validation remains outstanding.

headline: Mistral Opens a Trillion-Parameter Model
lede: Mistral Large 4 brings multimodal input, explicit reasoning, and tool use to an open-weight mixture-of-experts model. Its adjustable reasoning modes frame capability as a cost-and-latency decision, not a single score.

headline: Cohere Funds a Sovereign Frontier Stack
lede: Cohere is raising up to C$7 billion to build models, cyber tools, and deployable agents for controlled environments. The strategy treats context, verification, state, and customer infrastructure as part of the product.

headline: Lean Formalizes a Challenge to ETH
lede: Anthropic’s released Lean development claims a subexponential algorithm for 3-SAT and therefore a refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis. The asymptotic result is mathematically consequential, though its practical constants make it an artifact of theory rather than an engineering tool.

headline: Lean Checks the Finite Simple Groups Theorem
lede: Axiom Math reports a 43.1-million-line formalization assembled from 108 milestones and hundreds of subtasks. The project also exposed gaps in the published proof record, replacing a disputed step with a mechanically checked alternative.

headline: OpenAI Builds a Layered Misalignment Monitor
lede: OpenAI combines activation probes, transcript reviewers, investigative agents, and telemetry to detect suspicious frontier-model behavior. The architecture favors cheap high-recall sensors first, then progressively deeper investigation and human intervention.

headline: AI Finds Bugs Faster Than Humans Fix Them
lede: Automated vulnerability discovery is moving the bottleneck from detection to triage, disclosure, patching, and deployment. The result is a security workload that grows faster than the maintainer communities responsible for absorbing it.
pullquote: The scarce resource is no longer finding flaws; it is getting the internet repaired.

headline: Infostealers Add an LLM Analyst
lede: Volta-Autodoxer feeds stolen credentials, sessions, receipts, and personal clues to commercial language models. The model ranks victims and assembles dossiers, while provider fallbacks make refusal an inconvenience rather than a defense.

headline: A Preview Sandbox Handed Over ChatGPT Accounts
lede: A cross-frame messaging flaw, an unsandboxed iframe, and a permissive content policy formed a browser-side compromise chain. Attackers could execute code in the ChatGPT origin, call private APIs, and exfiltrate signed-in users’ data.

headline: NVIDIA Shrinks Active Compute in Nemotron
lede: Nemotron 3.5 combines Mamba layers, Transformer attention, sparse experts, multimodal training, and tool interaction. Its design spends computation selectively, then uses quantization and speculative decoding to improve the economics of inference.

headline: A TPU Runs Inference Above Earth
lede: Google’s Suncatcher prototype brings a Gemma model and TPU into orbit, where power, radiation, heat, and communications become part of the computing problem. The longer-term experiment is a coordinated satellite cluster linked by optical communications.

headline: Agents Push GitHub Activity to New Heights
lede: GitHub reports 220 million merged pull requests and 7.38 billion commits per month in its 2026 snapshot. The figures indicate a dramatic increase in software activity, but they do not by themselves establish code quality or agent authorship.

headline: Figma Trains a Model to Edit Directly
lede: Figma teaches a specialized agent to convert natural-language requests into valid changes in the application’s native design format. Structural checks, visual judges, reinforcement learning, and designer review keep the canvas—not the prose—as the final test.

headline: DeepSeek Builds an Always-On Coding Agent
lede: dsh-superagent turns repository events into authorized work items, isolated sessions, and proposed pull requests. Its architecture separates triggering, execution, monitoring, and approval—the control plane required when coding agents stop waiting for prompts.

headline: FrontierCode Measures Mergeable Code
lede: FrontierCode 2.0 scores whether an agent understands the surrounding repository, not merely whether it satisfies a stated request. More files, deeper regressions, and stricter thoroughness criteria push leading scores down while making the benchmark more representative of real review.

headline: Base Models Expose Hidden Model Personas
lede: Persona-header likelihood evaluation detects behavioral signals that prompted classifiers often miss. The result supports a provocative view of post-training: some latent objectives may be selected from structures already encoded during pretraining.

headline: A Benchmark Puts Financial Agents in Time
lede: Investor’s Last Exam evaluates research agents against historically frozen documents, market data, calculations, and assumptions. The scores show a familiar divide: systems can reconstruct the past more reliably than they can forecast the future.

headline: Meta Releases a Simulator for Wearable Assistants
lede: InteractiveWorld gives vision-language assistants a persistent world, a speaking human proxy, and explicit task predicates to satisfy. The simulator turns helpful-sounding guidance into a reproducible question: did the intended action actually occur?

headline: Qwenputer Turns Model State Into RAM
lede: Qwenputer embeds a deterministic RISC-V processor inside Qwen3.5 by repurposing recurrent state as addressable memory. Its verified traces and filesystem experiment show how neural components can be configured as exact computational machinery.

headline: Liquid AI Puts Voice and Vision On Device
lede: LFM3-Omni-2B combines language, vision, audio input, and speech generation in a 2.17-billion-parameter model. Its compact multimodal design points toward assistants that can see, hear, and respond locally rather than continuously sending perception to a server.
